html:
The Kingdom of Ireland was the state of Ireland from 1542 to 1800, ruled by the kings of England and later Great Britain and governed from Dublin Castle by a viceroy. The map shows it in 1715, 1783 and 1800.

Henry VIII created the title in 1542; the earlier English crown in Ireland had called itself only lord. After the wars of the 1600s, Catholic land was confiscated, and the country came to be run by a Protestant minority, the Protestant Ascendancy. The Penal Laws barred Catholics, the large majority, from parliament, the professions and buying land.

Ireland had its own parliament in Dublin, though it was long subject to London. In 1782 it won wider independence under the leadership of Henry Grattan. In 1798 the United Irishmen rose, hoping for French help, and the rebellion was put down with great bloodshed. The government answered with the Acts of Union, which abolished the Irish parliament and made Ireland part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 1801.
sum: The Kingdom of Ireland was the state of Ireland from 1542 to 1800, ruled by the kings of England and later Great Britain and governed from Dublin Castle by a viceroy. The map shows it in 1715, 1783 and 1800.
